day_shape: 76 items dominated by Strait of Hormuz diplomacy (Qatar mediation claims, UAE and Canada positioning, FT report on US covert mine-clearing), IAEA chief Grossi telling governors the agency is 'blind' to Iran's programme since June 2025, and IDF strikes in southern Lebanon reportedly killing 9-11 near Kfar Reman.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz diplomacy and posturing
threads.summary: Qatar's foreign ministry told CNN it is working to contain the Iran-US crisis with Hormuz reopening as priority, per Defa Press, while the UAE's Anwar Gargash rejected single-state control of the strait and Canada backed the US-France-UK reopening effort. Iran's foreign ministry threatened South Korea over any military participation, and the FT reported a covert four-month US Navy SEAL mine-clearing operation in the strait.

threads.label: IAEA visibility and regional nuclear file
threads.summary: IAEA Director-General Rafael Grossi told the Board of Governors the agency has been 'completely blind' to Iran's nuclear programme since at least June 2025, and Iran's spokesman Baghei threatened retaliation against any board resolution. Grossi also characterised the 2007 Syrian reactor destroyed by Israel as a fissile-material design, while the Jerusalem Post reported Saudi Arabia preparing IAEA access to its civil nuclear facilities.

threads.label: Southern Lebanon strikes and Hezbollah clashes
threads.summary: Lebanese media reported 11 killed and 5 wounded in overnight Israeli strikes on Kfar Reman, including two children and two paramedics, with the IDF saying it struck weapons stores and infrastructure after Hezbollah launched two explosive drones at troops in the Ali Taher Ridge area for the third time in a week. Two Golani Brigade soldiers were lightly wounded in a close-quarters clash near Beaufort Castle, with the IDF saying the gunman was killed.

threads.label: Gaza strikes and post-war architecture
threads.summary: The IDF announced killing Hamas Nukhba company commander Yusuf Aqila in Gaza City and two further operatives from PIJ and Hamas, and said it diverted a munition mid-air to avoid civilians. Kosovo signed on to the International Stabilization Force in Gaza, the US pushed a Board of Peace plan to decommission Hamas weapons, and UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese warned rubble clearance could destroy atrocity-crime evidence.

threads.label: Yemen-Saudi exchanges
threads.summary: Defa Press cited Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claiming Yemen's forces downed four Saudi drones over 24 hours, including a CH4 over al-Jawf, and targeted vehicles carrying ammunition to al-Wadia camp, alongside unverified claims of explosions at Saudi Aramco's Jizan facilities. The Jerusalem Post reported Yemeni government forces claiming limited gains against the Houthis near the Red Sea and Saudi border.

threads.label: Iran domestic economy and protests
threads.summary: Iran International reported oil workers protesting pay and benefits at Pars Oil and Gas offshore platforms and in Assaluyeh, while the Jerusalem Post noted small-scale demonstrations by retired telecoms workers, teachers and job seekers in Tehran and other cities. First Vice President Aref, via IRIB and Defa Press, said the petrol import subsidy would be phased out with only 15 percent of consumption subject to the new rate.

threads.label: Khamenei office messaging and mobilisation
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted a message accusing the 'Great Satan' of treaty violations following the signed Iran-US agreement and solicited public donations for war-affected citizens via card, IBAN and USSD channels. Defa Press announced a 313,000-person 'Iran Devotees' exercise scheduled for 27 Shahrivar in Tehran and reported a Baghdad ceremony honouring Khamenei's family hosted by the Popular Mobilisation Forces media department.
